cells.question: Q01

passages.locator: Section 5, definition of “frontier developer”, PDF pp. 3–4
passages.quote: “Frontier developer” means a person who trains, or … initiates the training of, a frontier model

passages.locator: Section 5, definition of “large frontier developer”, PDF p. 4
passages.quote: “Large frontier developer” means a frontier developer that, together with its affiliates, collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year.

cells.note: Two tiers in the act's defined terms. The transparency report (Section 10(c)(1)), incident reporting (Section 15(c)), the statements rule (Section 10(f)(1)) and the whistleblower duties (Section 20(a)–(d)) fall on frontier developers; the framework (Section 10(a)–(b)), the risk summaries in the transparency report (Section 10(c)(2)), the audit (Section 10(d)), internal-use summaries (Section 10(e)), the internal reporting process (Section 20(e)) and the disclosure statement (Section 18) fall on large frontier developers. “Person” is defined as a nongovernmental individual or organisation (Section 5). “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

cells.question: Q02

passages.locator: Section 5, definition of “frontier model”, first sentence, PDF p. 4
passages.quote: “Frontier model” means a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10 26 integer or floating-point operations.

passages.locator: Section 5, definition of “large frontier developer”, PDF p. 4
passages.quote: “Large frontier developer” means a frontier developer that, together with its affiliates, collectively had annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year.

cells.note: Model threshold: training compute greater than 10^26 operations, which under the second sentence of the definition includes the original training run and any subsequent fine-tuning, reinforcement learning or other material modifications the developer applies to a preceding foundation model. Developer threshold for the large tier: gross revenues with affiliates above $500 million in the preceding calendar year. The PDF prints the exponent as a superscript; its text layer gives “10 26”, which the quotation keeps (the figure is 10^26, as with the EU row's “1025”). Apart from that rendering, the quotation is word for word the one drafted on 2026-11-04 from the cross-family checker's copy (“10²⁶”).

cells.question: Q03

passages.quote: Beginning January 1, 2028, a large frontier developer … shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework

passages.locator: Section 5, definition of “frontier AI framework”, PDF p. 3
passages.quote: “Frontier AI framework” means documented technical and organizational protocols to manage, assess, and mitigate catastrophic risks.

cells.note: Applies to large frontier developers from 1 January 2028. Section 10(a)(1)–(10) lists the matters the framework describes, among them thresholds, mitigations, third-party assessment, cybersecurity for unreleased model weights, critical safety incidents and internal use; Section 10(b)(1) requires review and, as appropriate, update at least once a year. “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

cells.question: Q04

passages.quote: Beginning January 1, 2028, a large frontier developer … shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework
publish on its website the modified frontier AI framework and a justification for that modification within 30 days.

cells.note: Publication on the developer's website; a materially modified framework is published with a justification within 30 days. Section 10(g) permits redactions to protect trade secrets, cybersecurity, public safety or national security or to comply with law, with the character and justification of each redaction described. No provision found requiring the framework itself to be submitted to the Agency. “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: identify and assess whether a frontier model has capabilities that could pose a catastrophic risk
assessments of catastrophic risks from the frontier model conducted pursuant to the large frontier developer's frontier AI framework

cells.note: The framework, which a large frontier developer must implement and comply with, describes how the developer approaches defining and assessing thresholds to identify and assess whether a frontier model has capabilities that could pose a catastrophic risk (Section 10(a)(2)); the transparency report summarises assessments conducted under the framework and their results (Section 10(c)(2)(A)–(B)), and Section 10(e) requires summaries of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use to be sent to the Agency. The text sets no free-standing duty to assess or test each model, so the duty runs through the framework. Held: see the cell’s held record.

setAside.reason: Requires a summary of “any assessment” of internal-use risk to be sent to the Agency; it presupposes an assessment and does not itself require one.
A matter the framework describes (assessing and managing internal-use risk), not a free-standing duty to assess the model.

held.checkerReason: Large frontier developers must implement and comply with a framework addressing model-capability assessment (Section 10(a)(2)), mitigations based on those assessments and review of assessments and mitigations when deciding to deploy or use a model extensively internally (Section 10(a)(4)): a duty concerning frontier-model risks, not evidence that evaluations occurred (cross-family check 2026-11-04, item 5).
held.preparerReason: The act sets no free-standing duty to assess or test each model; the assessment duty runs through the framework, which describes how the developer “approaches” assessment. The wording is the same as California SB 53 § 22757.12(a), (a)(2) and (a)(4), which the pack records as partly and which the checker, reading it blind on 2026-11-02 (item 17), also read as partly.
held.recommendation: Partly, so that identical wording in the Illinois and California rows has one status (Quick: OK the recommendation). Alternatively stated, and California SB 53 Q05 then goes back to the checker for the same question.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: a large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance with the requirements of this Section.

cells.note: An annual independent audit of the large frontier developer's compliance with Section 10 (framework, transparency report, internal-use summaries, statements, redactions): an assessment of the developer's practices, not a test of the model. It begins on 1 January 2028 or 90 days after the developer first qualifies as a large frontier developer, whichever is later. The auditor must have no financial interest in the developer (or the developer in it), must have access to unredacted materials, reports on substantial compliance and internal controls (Section 10(d)(1)–(2)); a redacted copy and a summary are published and sent to the Agency and the Attorney General within 30 days (Section 10(d)(4)). The Agency and the Attorney General also review incident reports (Section 15(d)), a review of filings.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to … the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours of the frontier developer learning facts sufficient to establish a reasonable belief that a critical safety incident has occurred.
the frontier developer shall disclose that incident within 24 hours to an authority

cells.note: Applies to all frontier developers. Seventy-two hours to the Agency (the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security, Section 5) and the Attorney General; 24 hours to an appropriate authority, including law enforcement or public safety agencies, where the incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. “Critical safety incident” is defined in Section 5 (unauthorised access to model weights resulting in death or bodily injury, harm from a catastrophic risk, loss of control causing death or bodily injury, deceptive subversion of controls). “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new frontier model or a substantially modified version of an existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report

cells.note: Trigger: before or concurrently with deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model. Contents: website, contact mechanism, release date, languages, output modalities, intended uses and restrictions (Section 10(c)(1)(A)–(G)); a large frontier developer adds summaries of catastrophic-risk assessments, their results, third-party evaluators' involvement and other framework steps, in machine-readable form (Section 10(c)(2)–(3)). Publication within a system card or model card is deemed compliance (Section 10(c)(4)). Separately, large frontier developers send the Agency summaries of internal-use risk assessments every 3 months or on another schedule (Section 10(e)), and file an annual disclosure statement on the developer's identity, offices, owners and contacts (Section 18), which is not a report on each model. No labelling or watermark duty on outputs was found.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates … against a covered employee for disclosing, information to the Agency, Attorney General, a federal authority
a reasonable internal process through which a covered employee may anonymously disclose information

passages.locator: Section 90, Whistleblower Act Sec. 15(e), PDF p. 55
passages.quote: An employer may not take retaliatory action against an employee for disclosing or threatening to disclose in good faith any violation of the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act.

cells.note: A frontier developer may not adopt or enforce a rule, policy or contract that prevents, or retaliate against, disclosure by a “covered employee” (an employee responsible for assessing, managing or addressing the risk of critical safety incidents, Section 5) who has reasonable cause to believe the information shows a specific and substantial danger from a catastrophic risk or a violation of the act (Section 20(a)); notice of rights is required (Section 20(d)); large frontier developers provide an anonymous internal process with monthly updates (Section 20(e)). Section 90 amends the Whistleblower Act to protect any employee who discloses a violation of the act in good faith. “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

passages.quote: This Act takes effect January 1, 2027.

cells.question: Q12

passages.quote: Beginning January 1, 2028, a large frontier developer … shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework
Beginning on January 1, 2028 or 90 days after a developer first qualifies as a large frontier developer, whichever is later

cells.note: The framework duty applies from 1 January 2028 and the audit duty from 1 January 2028 or 90 days after first qualifying, whichever is later; both fall later than the act's effect date of 1 January 2027 (Section 99). Section 18(a)'s disclosure statement applies “beginning January 1, 2027”, the same day as the act. The transparency report, incident reporting and whistleblower duties set no date of their own. No transitional provision for models already deployed was found; the transparency report is triggered by deployment. “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

setAside.reason: “By January 1, 2029” sets the date of the Agency's annual report, not a developer duty.

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: does not exceed $1,000,000 for the first violation. For a subsequent violation, the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per violation.
a civil penalty of $1,000 for each day the person fails to file a disclosure

cells.note: Section 25(a): a civil penalty dependent on the severity of the violation, up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million per subsequent violation, for a large frontier developer that fails to publish or transmit a compliant document, makes a statement in violation of Section 10(f), fails to have the audit performed, fails to report a critical safety incident under Section 15 or fails to comply with its own framework. Section 18(e): for developing, deploying or operating without a current disclosure statement, false information or unpaid assessments, $1,000 per day plus the assessments owed, after notice and hearing, in addition to other penalties. Section 25(d) creates no private right of action.

cells.question: Q14

passages.quote: A civil penalty described in this Section shall be recovered in a civil action brought exclusively by the Attorney General.
the Agency may, after notice and hearing, levy civil penalties, fees, and costs

cells.note: The Attorney General recovers the Section 25 penalties. The Agency (the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security) levies the Section 18 disclosure penalties, receives incident reports, audit reports and internal-use summaries with the Attorney General, reviews incident reports with the Attorney General (Section 15(d)) and designates equivalent federal standards (Section 17(a)).

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: Beginning January 1, 2028, a large frontier developer … shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework

the frontier developer shall be deemed in compliance with this Act to the extent that the frontier developer meets the standards of, or complies with the requirements imposed or stated by, the designated federal law, regulation, or guidance document
including a system card or model card, shall be deemed in compliance with the applicable paragraph.

cells.note: Requires a developer framework, which describes how the developer approaches incorporating national standards, international standards and industry-consensus best practices (Section 10(a)(1)); penalises failure to comply with it (Section 25(a)). Deems compliance with a federal law, regulation or guidance document that the Agency designates as substantially equivalent, once the developer declares its intent to the Agency (Section 17(a)–(b)); failure to meet the designated standard is then a violation of the act (Section 17(b)(2)(B)). Deems a transparency report published within a system card or model card compliant (Section 10(c)(4)). Audits follow generally accepted auditing standards (Section 10(d)). “…” in the quotation stands for the running footer at a PDF page break; no words of the act are omitted.

omissions: Executive Order 2026-07 describes the act's duties (frameworks, annual audits, 72-hour incident reports, public disclosure). It is the Governor's description, not the act, so no cell quotes it; its passage on the signature is the row's standing evidence.

Section 80 (Freedom of Information Act, Sec. 7.5, three versions) adds an exemption for records exempt under the act; Section 15(f) lists them (incident reports, internal-use assessments, unredacted audit reports and audit materials, covered employee reports). Not used: disclosure of records held by public bodies is not one of the fifteen questions.
Section 35 (home rule) makes the regulation of frontier models an exclusive power of the State; Section 30 makes the duties cumulative with other law. Not used: no question asks about pre-emption.
